```python
import contextlib
import subprocess
import sysconfig

from rush.engines import vitest as vitest_engine

BUILD = ExecutionPermissions(build=True)


def _provisioned_vitest_project() -> Path:
    value = os.environ.get("RUSH_TEST_VITEST_PROJECT")
    assert value, "RUSH_TEST_VITEST_PROJECT must name a project with node_modules/.bin/vitest installed"
    project = Path(value)
    assert (project / "node_modules/.bin/vitest").is_file(), "provisioned Vitest missing"
    return project


def _venv_with_pytest(root):
    venv = root / ".venv"
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "venv", str(venv)], check=True)
    purelib = subprocess.run(
        [str(venv / "bin/python"), "-c", "import sysconfig;print(sysconfig.get_paths()['purelib'])"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
    (Path(purelib) / "rush_parent_env.pth").write_text(
        sysconfig.get_paths()["purelib"] + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return venv


def _python_files(root):
    (root / "pyproject.toml").write_text("[project]\nname='q04'\nversion='0.1'\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "tests").mkdir()
    (root / "tests/test_a.py").write_text("def test_a():\n    assert 1 == 1\n", encoding="utf-8")


def _vitest_files(root, body):
    (root / "package.json").write_text('{"name":"q04","private":true}', encoding="utf-8")
    (root / "a.test.ts").write_text("import {test,expect} from 'vitest'; " + body + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    os.symlink(_provisioned_vitest_project() / "node_modules", root / "node_modules")


def test_mixed_project_runs_both_suites(tmp_path):
    tmp_path = tmp_path.resolve()
    _python_files(tmp_path)
    venv = _venv_with_pytest(tmp_path)
    _vitest_files(tmp_path, "test('a',()=>expect(1).toBe(1))")
    result = TestTool().run(tmp_path, permissions=BUILD)
    rows = result["metadata"]["suites"]
    assert [r["suite"] for r in rows] == ["python", "javascript"]
    for row in rows:
        assert {k: row[k] for k in ("collected", "passed", "failed", "skipped", "status")} == {
            "collected": 1, "passed": 1, "failed": 0, "skipped": 0, "status": "ok"}
    assert rows[0]["environment"] == str(venv / "bin/python")
    assert rows[1]["environment"] == str(tmp_path / "node_modules/.bin/vitest")
    assert result["status"] == "ok" and result["metadata"]["partial"] is False


def test_project_venv_used(tmp_path):
    tmp_path = tmp_path.resolve()
    _python_files(tmp_path)
    venv = _venv_with_pytest(tmp_path)
    row = TestTool().run(tmp_path, suite="python", permissions=BUILD)["metadata"]["suites"][0]
    assert row["status"] == "ok"
    assert Path(row["environment"]).parent.parent == venv


def test_zero_collection_is_incomplete(tmp_path):
    tmp_path = tmp_path.resolve()
    (tmp_path / "pyproject.toml").write_text("[project]\nname='q04'\nversion='0.1'\n", encoding="utf-8")
    _venv_with_pytest(tmp_path)
    result = TestTool().run(tmp_path, suite="python", permissions=BUILD)
    row = result["metadata"]["suites"][0]
    assert result["status"] == "skipped" and result["metadata"]["partial"] is True
    assert {k: row[k] for k in ("collected", "passed", "failed", "skipped")} == {
        "collected": 0, "passed": 0, "failed": 0, "skipped": 0}


def test_environment_unresolved_never_falls_back(tmp_path):
    tmp_path = tmp_path.resolve()
    _python_files(tmp_path)
    (tmp_path / "package.json").write_text('{"name":"q04","private":true}', encoding="utf-8")
    result = TestTool().run(tmp_path, permissions=BUILD)
    assert result["metadata"]["subprocess_count"] == 0
    for row in result["metadata"]["suites"]:
        assert (row["status"], row["reason"], row["environment"]) == (
            "skipped", "environment_unresolved", "unresolved")
    assert result["status"] == "skipped" and result["metadata"]["partial"] is True


def test_vitest_fresh_report_cases(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    tmp_path = tmp_path.resolve()
    cases = {
        "pass": ("test('a',()=>expect(1).toBe(1))", ("ok", 1, 1, 0, 0)),
        "fail": ("test('a',()=>expect(1).toBe(2))", ("fail", 1, 0, 1, 0)),
        "skip": ("test.skip('a',()=>expect(1).toBe(1))", ("skipped", 1, 0, 0, 1)),
    }
    for name, (body, expected) in cases.items():
        root = tmp_path / name
        root.mkdir()
        _vitest_files(root, body)
        result = TestTool().run(root, suite="javascript", permissions=BUILD)
        row = result["metadata"]["suites"][0]
        assert (row["status"], row["collected"], row["passed"], row["failed"], row["skipped"]) == expected, name
        if name == "fail":
            assert result["findings"][0]["message"].startswith("AssertionError")
    absent = tmp_path / "absent"
    absent.mkdir()
    _vitest_files(absent, "")
    (absent / "a.test.ts").unlink()
    row = TestTool().run(absent, suite="javascript", permissions=BUILD)["metadata"]["suites"][0]
    assert (row["status"], row["collected"], row["passed"], row["failed"], row["skipped"]) == (
        "skipped", 0, 0, 0, 0)

    engine = vitest_engine.VitestEngine()
    monkeypatch.setattr(vitest_engine.VitestEngine, "version", lambda _self: "5.0.2")

    def fake_run(report_text):
        def run(argv, **_kwargs):
            out = next(a.split("=", 1)[1] for a in argv if a.startswith("--outputFile="))
            if report_text is not None:
                Path(out).write_text(report_text, encoding="utf-8")
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, stdout="", stderr="")
        return run

    corrupt = json.dumps({"testResults": [], "numTotalTests": 1, "numPassedTests": 1,
                          "numFailedTests": 0, "numPendingTests": 0, "numTodoTests": 0,
                          "success": True})
    for label, text in (("corrupt totals", corrupt), ("malformed", "{"), ("missing", None)):
        monkeypatch.setattr(vitest_engine, "run_subprocess", fake_run(text))
        raw = engine.run(tmp_path, [], cwd=tmp_path)
        assert engine.normalize(raw, tmp_path, "test")["status"] == "error", label

    stale_dir = tmp_path / "stale-report"
    stale_dir.mkdir()
    (stale_dir / "report.json").write_text(corrupt, encoding="utf-8")
    launched = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(vitest_engine, "run_subprocess", lambda argv, **_kw: launched.append(argv))
    monkeypatch.setattr(vitest_engine.tempfile, "TemporaryDirectory",
                        lambda prefix: contextlib.nullcontext(str(stale_dir)))
    raw = engine.run(tmp_path, [], cwd=tmp_path)
    assert launched == [] and engine.normalize(raw, tmp_path, "test")["status"] == "error"
```

```markdown
Every test, version and environment subprocess runs with cwd=project_root
(run_engine(..., cwd=project_root)). Pytest argv is exactly
[interpreter, "-m", "pytest", *(selected_nodes or [str(project_root)]), "--tb=line", "-q"];
```

#### Q04-08 — MCP strict-bool rejection has no mechanism
- Severity: major
- Plan location: `:52–53` ("bool/string budgets"), `:120` ("reject string/integer bool coercion").
- Problem:
  - Plain `bool` and `int` annotations in `TestTool.__call__` are coerced by FastMCP's pydantic model.
  - The plan names no mechanism.
  - The reviewer's mechanism (a `rush_test` `_ToolSpec` in `request_models.py`) does not fit. `request_models.py` is bespoke to project, scan and memory: `REQUEST_MODEL_TOOLS` is a frozenset of those three, and its envelope normalization wraps arguments as `{"request": …}`, which `rush_test.__call__` does not accept.
  - A simpler mechanism works and was tested: annotate the `__call__` parameters with `StrictBool`, `StrictInt`, `StrictStr` and `Literal`. `make_tool_wrapper` derives the published signature from `inspect.signature(tool.__call__, eval_str=True)` (`tool_registry.py:331`).
- Evidence (real server, in-process client session, typed `__call__` as in P1):
  - Valid call: ok.
  - `allow_build="true"`: isError, "Input should be a valid boolean".
  - `max_subprocesses="7"`: isError. `max_subprocesses=True`: isError.
  - `suite="ruby"`: isError. `test_paths=[1]`: isError.
  - Control: with the current plain `bool`, `allow_build="true"` is accepted.
- Fix for Codex: replace plan line 120's fragment `reject string/integer bool coercion;` with:

```markdown
reject coercion by typing TestTool.__call__ with pydantic StrictBool (allow_build,
allow_slow), StrictInt (max_subprocesses), list[StrictStr] (test_paths, changed_files),
StrictStr (minimize_order_failure, image_ref) and Literal (suite, test_environment); FastMCP
derives the published schema and validation from that signature
(mcp_support/tool_registry.py:331), so no request_models.py entry is added.
```

Add to the `tests/test_mcp.py` deliverable:

```python
def test_rush_test_rejects_coerced_arguments(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "pyproject.toml").write_text("[project]\nname='x'\nversion='0.1'\n", encoding="utf-8")
    for arguments in ({"allow_build": "true"}, {"allow_build": 1}, {"max_subprocesses": "7"},
                      {"max_subprocesses": True}, {"suite": "ruby"}, {"test_paths": [1]}):
        result = _call_rush_test(tmp_path, arguments)  # the plan's _test_stdio helper, returning the CallToolResult
        assert result.isError is True, arguments
```
with `_call_rush_test` defined as a variant of `_test_stdio` that returns the response object instead of parsing JSON.
- Fix verification: `rtk grep -n "StrictBool\|test_rush_test_rejects_coerced_arguments" docs/phase-plans/command-tdd-2026-10-01/04-rush-test.md`.

  - Dropped receipt fields: the audit receipt carries `attempts` (2509, 2556) and `environment_digest` (2498). The plan's key list at `:174–176` has neither, and the RED dropped the `attempts == 2` assert.

  - Altered shared signature: the plan's W18 interface (`:130–133`) drops `workdir_rel` and `environment` and adds `max_process_launches`. The audit says the provider is shared with W19 and W21 (13812).

- Fix for Codex: replace plan lines 130–136, from `Required proposed interface: run_isolated_argv(root:Path,scratch:Path,*,` through `not implemented; W18 owner must supply it before X1 acceptance.`, with:

```markdown
Required proposed interface (additive to audit 13824; W18/W19/W21 callers unchanged):
run_isolated_argv(root, scratch, *, runtime_path, image_ref, entrypoint, argv, timeout_s,
workdir_rel=".", environment=None, max_process_launches=None) returns an IsolatedProcess
dataclass (returncode, stdout, stderr, process_launches, receipt) and raises IsolationUnavailable
(audit 13821) and ProcessBudgetExhausted(process_launches) before the launch that would exceed
max_process_launches. Callers that omit the new keyword read only .returncode/.stdout/.stderr.
The provider reserves a launch before each environment/backend/test subprocess; the receipt
counts all launches. Calling it with remaining budget <= 0 is prohibited. Not implemented; the
W18 acceptance decision under Checks governs X1.
```

Replace plan lines 174–179 (`metadata.interaction_reproducer has status, …` through `target_fails_alone and errors must not publish one_deletion_minimal.`) with:

```markdown
metadata.interaction_reproducer has: status, ordered_nodes, minimality, subprocess_count,
attempts, process_receipts, observations, environment_digest, and reason only when present.
Each process receipt records argv, returncode (null when the provider raised
ProcessBudgetExhausted) and process_launches, including validation/control processes.
subprocess_count equals their sum and cannot exceed max_subprocesses. attempts = the baseline plus
every reduction candidate evaluated (cached included), excluding the target-alone check (the
audit's two-node fixture gives attempts == 2). observations lists every evaluated sequence with
target_failed and cached. environment_digest = sha256 of the sorted-key JSON of {image_ref,
runtime_sha256, sources: {relative path: sha256}}. IsolationUnavailable => status "skipped",
reason "isolation_unavailable", minimality null, receipts retained. Non-reproduction,
target_fails_alone and errors never publish one_deletion_minimal.
```

### REFUTED sub-claims (inside otherwise valid findings)

- Q04-01: "audit probes call `run_subprocess` without `ownership_kwargs`, contradicting plan line 65." Refuted. `run_subprocess` reads the ambient owned scope that `executor.py:602` sets (`subprocesses.py:894–897`), so direct probes inherit ownership. No `owner_instance_id`/`run_id` run parameters are needed.
- Q04-06: the `metadata.scope` mention. The plan does not touch it. The reviewer's `partial` rule is wrong, as shown.
- Q04-09: `tests/test_pytest_reference.py` and `tests/test_engines.py` do not break while `interpreter` stays optional.
- Q04-13: "Path escape errors contradicts audit 2217". The audit raises `ContainmentError` at 2216 for escapes.

### Missed issues (found while verifying, evidence in the findings above)

1. Absolute graph path rejected (Q04-04). Plan RED #1 passes `tmp_path / "test-graph.json"`, and `PhysicalRoot.open_contained` raises `ABSOLUTE_PATH_DISALLOWED`, so it can never reach `ok`. Fixed in P1 `select_graph_tests`.
2. Existing tests broken beyond the reviewer's list (Q04-09): `tests/test_project_python.py:101,184,217` and `tests/test_phase70_t17.py:563–578,638–660`. The Q04-09 fix schedules them.

  ```python
  def test_verified_sbom_consumer_requires_digest_and_records_child(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
      (tmp_path / "package.json").write_text('{"name":"fixture"}')
      sbom = tmp_path / "sbom.json"
      sbom.write_text(json.dumps({"bomFormat": "CycloneDX", "specVersion": "1.5",
          "components": [{"type": "library", "name": "demo", "version": "1.0",
                          "purl": "pkg:pypi/demo@1.0"}]}))
      digest = hashlib.sha256(sbom.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
      calls = []
      def checked(root, sbom_path, expected_sha256, *, permissions):
          calls.append((root, sbom_path, expected_sha256, permissions.network))
          assert hashlib.sha256((root / sbom_path).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == expected_sha256
          return {"tool": "security", "engine": "osv-querybatch", "engine_version": None,
              "status": "warn", "duration_ms": 0, "summary": "one advisory",
              "findings": [{"path": "sbom.json", "line": 0, "rule": "OSV-1",
                            "severity": "warn", "message": "demo vulnerable"}],
              "metadata": {"sbom_sha256": expected_sha256}}
      monkeypatch.setattr("rush.tools.security.audit_verified_sbom", checked)
      monkeypatch.setattr("rush.tools.common.engine_on_path", lambda binary: False)
      with patch("rush.tools.security.run_engine", side_effect=lambda e, p, a, **k: _child(e.name)):
          result = SecurityTool().run(tmp_path, sbom_path=Path("sbom.json"), sbom_sha256=digest,
                                      permissions=ExecutionPermissions(network=True))
          unpaired = SecurityTool().run(tmp_path, sbom_path=Path("sbom.json"))
      assert calls[0] == (tmp_path.resolve(), Path("sbom.json"), digest, True)
      assert len(calls) == 1
      row = next(r for r in result["metadata"]["scope"]["dependencies"]
                 if r["relative_path"] == "sbom.json")
      assert (row["kind"], row["engine"], row["state"]) == ("cyclonedx_sbom", "osv-querybatch", "audited")
      assert any(f["rule"] == "OSV-1" for f in result["findings"])
      assert (unpaired["status"], unpaired["summary"]) == (
          "error", "sbom_path and sbom_sha256 required together")
  ```

#### Q05-21 — "Offline database digest" acceptance has no source API
- Severity: major
- Plan location: PLAN:127-130 ("recorded version and offline database digest").
- Problem:
  - Neither revision computes an advisory database identity. `osv.py` hard-codes `"database_freshness": "unknown-offline"`, even though T14 says "Record advisory DB identity/freshness".
  - The reviewer's fix describes the location only as "per the docs URL" and hashes "the directory".
  - The documented layout (verified below) is `{local_db_dir}/osv-scanner/{ecosystem}/all.zip`, with `{local_db_dir}` taken from `OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY`, else `os.UserCacheDir()`, else `os.TempDir()`.
- Evidence:
  - `66c6c79:src/rush/engines/osv.py:177` (the only `database_freshness` in `src`; line 154 at c78e445).
  - The T14 plan line `phase-70-agent-adoption-and-usability-plan.md:199` ("Record advisory DB identity/freshness").
  - Fetched https://google.github.io/osv-scanner/usage/offline-mode/ this session: the layout and lookup order above.
  - macOS: `~/Library/Caches/osv-scanner` exists on this machine (empty).
  - `osv-scanner --version` prints `osv-scanner version: 2.4.0`.
- Fix for Codex (DECISION D5, flagged). Replace PLAN:128-129 ("recorded version and offline database digest.") with:
  ```text
  recorded osv-scanner version (the osv-scanner engine entry's "version") and `advisory_db` identity.
  Add to security.py and attach the result as `advisory_db` on every metadata.engines entry whose
  engine is "osv-scanner":
      def _osv_database_identity():
          bases = []
          override = os.environ.get("OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY")
          if override:
              bases.append(Path(override))
          bases.append(_user_cache_dir())      # Go os.UserCacheDir: macOS ~/Library/Caches,
                                               # Linux $XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache, Windows %LocalAppData%
          bases.append(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()))
          for base in bases:
              root = base / "osv-scanner"
              archives = sorted(root.glob("*/all.zip")) if root.is_dir() else []
              if archives:
                  digest = hashlib.sha256()
                  for archive in archives:
                      file_digest = hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                      digest.update(archive.parent.name.encode() + b"\0" + file_digest.encode() + b"\n")
                  return {"path": str(root), "sha256": digest.hexdigest(),
                          "ecosystems": [a.parent.name for a in archives], "reason": None}
          return {"path": None, "sha256": None, "ecosystems": [], "reason": "advisory_db_not_found"}
  When sha256 is null the osv rows are db_unavailable; a digest is never fabricated. The real-format
  acceptance asserts advisory_db.sha256 is a 64-hex string for a provisioned database and null with
  reason advisory_db_not_found when none exists.
  ```
- Fix verification: `rtk grep -n "advisory_db" PLAN` ≥ 1. After GREEN, `tests/test_security.py::test_osv_database_identity_missing_is_null` (monkeypatch `OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY` and `HOME`/`XDG_CACHE_HOME` to an empty temp dir and assert `{"sha256": None, "reason": "advisory_db_not_found"}`) passes. Write that test in the plan with the monkeypatches.

#### Q06-02 — `typecheck_config` resolution/containment root conflicts with shipped Phase 70 semantics
- Severity: blocker
- Plan location: `:32` ("typecheck_config: Path|None=None"), `:133–134` ("contract. File targets inside Git use verified git rev-parse --show-toplevel … parent directory."), `:166`, `:176`, `:220–221`, `:236`, `:267–268`, `:278`.
- Problem: Phase 70 types `typecheck_config` as `str | None`. The CLI Click callback anchors it with `os.path.abspath` against the invocation cwd. MCP anchors it via `_CWD_RELATIVE_ARGS`. The tool validates containment against `resolve_logical_root`, not the git toplevel. The plan's relative `Path("tsconfig.json")` and its git-toplevel rule contradict this. The plan's RED body gets `TYPECHECK_CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, and the parity test's CLI side resolves `tsconfig.json` against the rush-cli repo.
- Evidence:
  - 66c6c79 `typecheck.py:214–260` `_validate_config` (`Path(os.path.abspath(value))`; `PhysicalRoot(logical_root).open_contained(literal.relative_to(logical_root), …)`). `typecheck.py:198` `_logical_root` → `resolve_logical_root`.
  - 66c6c79 `catalog_commands.py:283–290` abspath callback ("anchored to the invocation cwd, exactly once"). `tool_registry.py:63` `"typecheck": ("typecheck_config",)`.
  - Probe at 66c6c79 with `typecheck_config="tsconfig.json"` and cwd elsewhere → `error TYPECHECK_CONFIG_NOT_FOUND …/tsconfig.json is not an existing regular file`.
  - Plan parity body at 66c6c79 (with `src` symlinked to the worktree): `AssertionError: assert 'error' == 'fail'` (plan line 287).
- Fix for Codex: Replace lines 32–34 with:
  ```
  Keep Phase 70's `typecheck_config: str | None = None`, `environment`,
  `allow_build`, `allow_cache_write`. Add caller_graph_path: str|None=None,
  explain_config_effect: str|None=None, runtime_path: str|None=None,
  image_ref: str|None=None and allow_slow: bool=False to TypecheckTool.__call__
  and run. Path-valued strings follow Phase 70 S12.7: CLI values are made
  absolute against the invocation cwd by the Click callback; MCP values are
  anchored by tool_registry._CWD_RELATIVE_ARGS["typecheck"], extended to
  ("typecheck_config", "caller_graph_path", "runtime_path"). The tool requires
  containment within the logical root (typecheck.py::_logical_root) for
  typecheck_config and caller_graph_path; runtime_path must be an absolute
  existing executable and is not containment-checked.
  ```
  Replace lines 133–134 (`contract. File targets inside Git use verified git rev-parse --show-toplevel / as containment/config-search root; non-Git file targets use parent directory.`) with:
  ```
  Containment and config-search root is Phase 70's logical root
  (typecheck.py::_logical_root -> invocation.targets.resolve_logical_root).
  ```
  In every RED body make these replacements:
  - `typecheck_config=Path("tsconfig.json")` → `typecheck_config=str(config)` (alias test, experiment test) or `str(tmp_path / "tsconfig.json")` (stale-graph args).
  - `typecheck_config=Path("override.json")` → `str(override)`.
  - `caller_graph_path=Path("callers.json")` → `str(tmp_path / "callers.json")`.
  - In the parity body, `"tsconfig.json"` → `str(tmp_path / "tsconfig.json")` on both the CLI and MCP sides.
- Fix verification: `rtk grep -n 'Path("tsconfig.json")\|Path("callers.json")\|Path("override.json")\|git rev-parse --show-toplevel' docs/phase-plans/command-tdd-2026-10-01/06-rush-typecheck.md` returns no matches. The corrected bodies passed against the patched scratch copy.

#### Q06-09 — Denied build/slow grant asserted as `error`; audit and runtime say `skipped`
- Severity: major
- Plan location: `:38` ("Invalid grant type/config escape => error."), `:86`, `:240–241` (`assert denied["status"] == "error"`).
- Problem: The audit's experiment returns `skipped_result(self.name, None, "build_or_slow_denied")` for missing grants (audit:3174–3175). The shared runtime also returns `skipped` for ungranted permissions (c78e445 `subprocesses.py:1105–1108`; 66c6c79 `subprocesses.py:1621–1639`). The plan merges "denied" with "invalid type" and asserts `error` for denial.
- Correction to the reviewer's premise: Phase 70's `_GRANTS` StrictBool in `mcp_support/request_models.py` covers the workflow request models, not `rush_typecheck`. Over actual stdio MCP at 66c6c79 `allow_cache_write` behaves as follows:
  - `"true"` and `1` → treated as granted (tsc ran, `fail`);
  - `"false"` → `skipped`;
  - `null` → protocol-level `isError=True` ("Input should be a valid boolean"), not a ToolResult.
  So plan line 86 (real booleans required) is unmet for typecheck at 66c6c79 and must be built here.
- Evidence:
  - Executed stdio calls, and a FastMCP experiment: a parameter annotated `pydantic.StrictBool` rejects `"true"`, `1` and `None`; a parameter annotated `bool` accepts `"true"` and `1`.
  - `tool_registry.py` builds the public signature from `TypecheckTool.__call__`'s own annotations (`_with_view_params`/`_callable_signature`), so a `StrictBool` annotation reaches MCP.
  - The permission-denial summary format is `f"requires permission: {', '.join(missing)}"` (comma-joined), and `skipped_result` prefixes `skipped: `. The reviewer's assertion `"requires permission: --allow-build --allow-slow"` (no comma) would fail.
- Fix for Codex: Replace line 38 with:
  ```
  Existing run(config=None) preserved. Grants are strict booleans:
  TypecheckTool.__call__ annotates allow_build/allow_slow/allow_cache_write as
  pydantic StrictBool, so MCP rejects "true", 1, null, lists and objects before
  the tool runs ("Input should be a valid boolean", tool-level isError); run()
  itself returns status "error", metadata.error.code "INVALID_PERMISSION_TYPE"
  and spawns nothing for any non-bool grant (direct Python calls). A valid false
  grant never authorizes work. explain_config_effect without both allow_build
  and allow_slow => status "skipped", summary
  "skipped: typecheck: explain_config_effect requires permission: --allow-build, --allow-slow",
  no baseline run and no trial process. Escaped typecheck_config /
  caller_graph_path => status "error" with TYPECHECK_CONFIG_OUTSIDE_ROOT /
  TYPECHECK_CALLER_GRAPH_OUTSIDE_ROOT.
  ```
  Replace `assert denied["status"] == "error"` (line 241) with:
  ```python
      assert denied["status"] == "skipped"
      assert "requires permission: --allow-build, --allow-slow" in denied["summary"]
      assert "config_experiment" not in denied.get("metadata", {})
  ```
  Add this test (validated against the patched scratch copy; it fails at 66c6c79 because `run(allow_cache_write="true")` proceeds as truthy):
  ```python
  def test_grants_must_be_booleans(tmp_path):
      src = tmp_path / "src"; src.mkdir()
      a = src / "a.ts"; a.write_text("export const v: number = 1;\n")
      for value in ("true", 1, None, [True]):
          r = TypecheckTool().run(a, allow_cache_write=value)
          assert r["status"] == "error"
          assert r["metadata"]["error"]["code"] == "INVALID_PERMISSION_TYPE"
  ```
- Fix verification: `rtk grep -n 'denied\["status"\] == "error"' docs/phase-plans/command-tdd-2026-10-01/06-rush-typecheck.md` returns no matches. Code is in Q06-24.

  ```python
  def test_typecheck_options_cli_mcp_parity(tmp_path):
      import hashlib, json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
      from pathlib import Path
      import anyio
      from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
      from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client
      project = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
      env = {**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(project / "src")}
      assert shutil.which("tsc"), "Installed version-pinned tsc required"
      src = tmp_path / "src"; src.mkdir()
      a = src / "a.ts"; b = src / "b.ts"
      a.write_text("export const value: string = null;\n")
      b.write_text('import {value} from "./a"; export const caller = value;\n')
      cfg = tmp_path / "tsconfig.json"
      cfg.write_text(json.dumps({"compilerOptions": {"strict": True}, "include": ["src/*.ts"]}))
      edges = [{"diagnostic": "TS2322@src/a.ts:1", "caller": "src/b.ts::caller", "evidence_id": "fixture-edge-1"}]
      graph = tmp_path / "callers.json"
      graph.write_text(json.dumps({"version": 1, "complete": True, "sources": {
          f"src/{p.name}": hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in (a, b)}, "edges": edges}))
      git_fixture(tmp_path)
      def cli(*extra):
          proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "rush.cli", "typecheck", str(tmp_path), *extra, "--json"],
              cwd=project, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
          return proc, (json.loads(proc.stdout) if proc.stdout.strip() else None)
      async def exchange(arguments):
          params = StdioServerParameters(command=sys.executable, args=["-m", "rush.cli", "mcp", "serve"], cwd=project, env=env)
          with tempfile.TemporaryFile(mode="w+", encoding="utf-8") as errlog:
              with anyio.fail_after(180):
                  async with stdio_client(params, errlog=errlog) as (read, write):
                      async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
                          await session.initialize()
                          response = await session.call_tool("rush_typecheck", {"path": str(tmp_path), **arguments})
                          return response.isError, response.content[0].text
      proc, left = cli("--typecheck-config", str(cfg), "--caller-graph-path", str(graph), "--allow-cache-write")
      assert proc.returncode == 1, proc.stderr
      is_error, text = anyio.run(exchange, {"typecheck_config": str(cfg), "caller_graph_path": str(graph), "allow_cache_write": True})
      assert is_error is False
      right = json.loads(text)
      assert (left["tool"], left["status"]) == (right["tool"], right["status"]) == ("typecheck", "fail")
      keys = ("path", "line", "column", "rule", "severity", "message")
      assert [{k: f.get(k) for k in keys} for f in left["findings"]] == [{k: f.get(k) for k in keys} for f in right["findings"]]
      assert [f["rule"] for f in left["findings"]] == ["TS2322"]
      assert left["metadata"]["diagnostic_callers"] == right["metadata"]["diagnostic_callers"] == {"status": "assessed", "edges": edges}
      assert left["metadata"]["scope"]["configuration_files"] == right["metadata"]["scope"]["configuration_files"] == [str(cfg)]
      bad_error, bad_text = anyio.run(exchange, {"typecheck_config": str(cfg), "allow_cache_write": "true"})
      assert bad_error is True and "valid boolean" in bad_text
      proc2, left2 = cli("--typecheck-config", str(cfg), "--allow-cache-write", "--explain-config-effect", "TS2322@src/a.ts:1")
      assert proc2.returncode == 0, proc2.stderr
      _, text2 = anyio.run(exchange, {"typecheck_config": str(cfg), "allow_cache_write": True, "explain_config_effect": "TS2322@src/a.ts:1"})
      right2 = json.loads(text2)
      assert left2["status"] == right2["status"] == "skipped"
      assert left2["summary"] == right2["summary"]
  ```

Add a `## Proposed production code (66c6c79 base)` section containing:
  ```python
  # imports at top of src/rush/tools/typecheck.py
  import hashlib, json, subprocess, tempfile                      # plus existing os
  from pydantic import StrictBool
  from ..permissions import ExecutionPermissions, build_execution_metadata, check_permissions

  _CALLER_UNASSESSED = {"status": "unassessed", "reason": "caller_graph_stale_or_invalid", "edges": []}
  _EXPERIMENT_OPTIONS = ("strictNullChecks", "noUnusedLocals", "noImplicitAny", "exactOptionalPropertyTypes")
  _EXPERIMENT_TIMEOUT_S = 300

  def _diagnostic_key(finding, logical_root):
      reported = Path(str(finding.get("path", "")))
      source = Path(os.path.realpath(reported if reported.is_absolute() else logical_root / reported))
      root = Path(os.path.realpath(logical_root))
      if source != root and root not in source.parents:
          return None
      return f"{finding.get('rule')}@{source.relative_to(root).as_posix()}:{finding.get('line')}"

  def _validate_caller_graph(graph_path, logical_root, findings):
      physical = PhysicalRoot(logical_root)
      try:
          graph_file = physical.open_contained(graph_path.relative_to(logical_root), purpose="read")
      except (ValueError, ContainmentError):
          return _config_error("TYPECHECK_CALLER_GRAPH_OUTSIDE_ROOT",
                               f"typecheck: --caller-graph-path {graph_path} lies outside {logical_root}")
      try:
          graph = json.loads(graph_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
          sources, edges = graph["sources"], graph["edges"]
          if not (graph["version"] == 1 and graph["complete"] is True
                  and isinstance(sources, dict) and sources and isinstance(edges, list)):
              return dict(_CALLER_UNASSESSED)
          for relative, digest in sources.items():
              if not (isinstance(relative, str) and isinstance(digest, str)):
                  return dict(_CALLER_UNASSESSED)
              data = physical.open_contained(relative, purpose="read").read_bytes()
              if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != digest:
                  return dict(_CALLER_UNASSESSED)
          keys = {k for k in (_diagnostic_key(f, logical_root) for f in findings) if k}
          rows = []
          for edge in edges:
              if not (isinstance(edge, dict) and all(isinstance(edge.get(n), str)
                      for n in ("diagnostic", "caller", "evidence_id"))):
                  return dict(_CALLER_UNASSESSED)
              if (edge["diagnostic"].rsplit("@", 1)[-1].rsplit(":", 1)[0] not in sources
                      or edge["caller"].split("::", 1)[0] not in sources):
                  return dict(_CALLER_UNASSESSED)
              if edge["diagnostic"] in keys:
                  rows.append(edge)
          return {"status": "assessed", "edges": rows}
      except (OSError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, ContainmentError):
          return dict(_CALLER_UNASSESSED)

  def _experiment_config(logical_root, owner, target, runtime_path, image_ref):
      from ..engines.tsc import parse_tsc_output
      from ..runtime.isolated_process import IsolationUnavailable, run_isolated_argv  # W18 (Q06-07)
      root = Path(os.path.realpath(logical_root))
      rel_config = Path(os.path.realpath(owner)).relative_to(root).as_posix()
      source = Path(os.path.realpath(target["path"])).relative_to(root).as_posix()
      target_key = (target["rule"], source, target["line"], target["message"])
      counted = 1                                   # the baseline run that produced `target`
      def trial(scratch, option):
          argv = ["--noEmit", "--project", f"/work/{rel_config}", "--pretty", "false", f"--{option}", "false"]
          try:
              proc = run_isolated_argv(root, scratch, runtime_path=runtime_path, image_ref=image_ref,
                  entrypoint="/usr/local/bin/tsc", argv=argv, timeout_s=_EXPERIMENT_TIMEOUT_S)
          except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
              return {"option": option, "value": "false", "status": "error", "target_present": True}
          parsed = parse_tsc_output((proc.stdout or "") + (proc.stderr or ""), Path("/work"))
          present = any((d["rule"], Path(d["path"]).relative_to("/work").as_posix(), d["line"], d["message"])
                        == target_key for d in parsed.diagnostics if d.get("path"))
          status = "ok" if proc.returncode == 0 else "fail" if parsed.diagnostics else "error"
          return {"option": option, "value": "false", "status": status, "target_present": present}
      observations, suppressing = [], []
      try:
          with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".rush-typecheck-exp-", dir=root.parent) as scratch:
              for option in _EXPERIMENT_OPTIONS:
                  observations.append(trial(scratch, option)); counted += 1
              for item in list(observations):
                  if item["status"] in ("ok", "fail") and not item["target_present"]:
                      again = trial(scratch, item["option"]); counted += 1
                      if (again["status"], again["target_present"]) == (item["status"], False):
                          suppressing.append(item["option"])
      except IsolationUnavailable:
          return {"status": "skipped", "reason": "isolation_unavailable", "observations": []}
      return {"status": "assessed", "diagnostic_id": _diagnostic_key(target, logical_root),
              "observations": observations, "suppressing_options": suppressing,
              "source_digest": hashlib.sha256(Path(target["path"]).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
              "config_digest": hashlib.sha256(Path(owner).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
              "checker_process_count": counted, "policy_recommendation": "none"}
  ```
  `__call__` (66c6c79 lines 323–337) becomes:

     ```python
     def _explain(self, result, logical_root, diagnostic_id, runtime_path, image_ref):
         relative = diagnostic_id.rsplit("@", 1)[-1].rsplit(":", 1)[0]
         real_root = Path(os.path.realpath(logical_root))
         real_source = Path(os.path.realpath(real_root / relative))
         if real_source != real_root and real_root not in real_source.parents:
             return _config_error("TYPECHECK_DIAGNOSTIC_OUTSIDE_ROOT", f"typecheck: {diagnostic_id} lies outside {logical_root}")
         target = next((f for f in result["findings"]
                        if _diagnostic_key(f, logical_root) == diagnostic_id
                        and str(f.get("rule", "")).startswith("TS")), None)
         if target is None:
             return _config_error("TYPECHECK_DIAGNOSTIC_NOT_REPRODUCED",
                                  f"typecheck: {diagnostic_id} was not reproduced by the baseline run")
         owner = (target.get("extensions") or {}).get("config")
         if not owner:
             return _config_error("TYPECHECK_DIAGNOSTIC_NO_OWNER", f"typecheck: {diagnostic_id} has no owning tsconfig")
         return _experiment_config(logical_root, Path(owner), dict(target), runtime_path, image_ref)
     ```
  The CLI options go into `_TOOL_CLI_OPTIONS["typecheck"]` per Q06-18, and `_CWD_RELATIVE_ARGS["typecheck"]` per Q06-02.

#### M2 — `scripts/sync_docs.py --check` is a CI gate that the plan's new options, docs and ADR will trip

  So the plan, the reviewer's docs fixes and the new options all fail CI unless that report is updated.

#### Q07-01 — Knip rejects positional file args; plan's "nonzero ⇒ error" makes every JS scan `error`
- Severity: blocker
- Plan location: `07-rush-dead.md:40-42` ("Knip uses --reporter json --no-exit-code; require object with issues list; normalize unused export by file/name/line. Nonzero or malformed JSON => error.")
- Problem:
  - `DeadTool.run` forwards `[str(target) for target in targets]` (`dead.py:54`). `KnipEngine.run` appends them (`knip.py:28`).
  - Knip 6.35.1 exits 1 on any positional argument, even with `--no-exit-code`.
  - Today the text regex finds nothing in the usage text, so a real unused export is reported `ok` with 0 findings.
  - Implemented as the plan words it, every JS/TS scan becomes `error`.
- Evidence:
  - `knip --reporter json --no-exit-code lib.js` gave rc 1 and stderr `Unexpected argument 'lib.js'. This command does not take positional arguments`. The absolute-path form fails the same way.
  - With cwd at the project root and no args, rc was 0 and stdout was `{"issues":[{"file":"lib.js",…,"exports":[{"name":"unused","line":2,"col":14,"pos":36}],…}]}`.
  - `python -m rush.cli dead <tmp> --json` returned `status ok findings []` at c78e445 and at 66c6c79 (engines `[('knip','ok',None)]`). The unused export was missed at both.
- Fix for Codex: replace plan lines 40-42 (from `Knip uses --reporter json` through `audit observed Knip6.35.1 only.`) with the text below. This also applies the Q07-06 reason names and Q07-18 truncation rule.
  ```text
  Knip 6.35.1 rejects positional arguments (exit 1, "Unexpected argument"). src/rush/engines/knip.py:
  new module function knip_root(path: Path) -> Path = nearest directory at or above
  (path if path.is_dir() else path.parent), resolved, that contains package.json, else that start directory.
  KnipEngine.run ignores its args and cwd parameters and runs
  [resolve_binary(self.binary) or self.binary, "--reporter", "json", "--no-exit-code"] with cwd=knip_root(path).
  KnipEngine.normalize (imports: json; error_result added to the tools.common import):
    exit_code != 0 => error_result(..., terminal_reason="nonzero_exit");
    stdout ending "[TRUNCATED]", non-JSON stdout, missing/non-list "issues", an issue lacking str "file",
    a category that is not a list, or an item lacking str "name" or int "line" => terminal_reason="invalid_engine_output".
  Categories read per issue (all always present in 6.35.1 output): exports, types, enumMembers, namespaceMembers
  (message "Unused {kind}: {name}") and files, dependencies, devDependencies, optionalPeerDependencies, unlisted,
  unresolved, binaries, duplicates (list of lists, flattened), catalog, catalogReferences (message "Knip {kind}: {name}").
  An item without "line" gets line 1 (file-level). Finding {"path": issue["file"], "line", "rule": f"knip/{kind}",
  "severity": "warn"}. An issue is kept only when (knip_root(path)/issue["file"]).resolve() is_relative_to(path.resolve()).
  ```

     ```python
         pattern = re.compile(r"^(?P<path>.+?):(?P<line>\d+): (?P<message>.*)$")
         stdout, code = raw.get("stdout", ""), raw.get("exit_code")
         if code not in (0, 3) and not stdout.strip():

         parsed = [pattern.fullmatch(line) for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]

         return ToolResult(tool=tool_name, engine=self.name, engine_version=self.version(), status="warn" if findings else "ok",
             duration_ms=raw.get("duration_ms", 0), summary=f"vulture: {len(findings)} unused item(s)", findings=findings, raw=None)
     ```

  ```python
  def _tree(root):
      return sorted((p.relative_to(root).as_posix(), hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest())
                    for p in root.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and ".git" not in p.parts)

  def _probe_project(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
      source = tmp_path/"app.py"; source.write_text("def callback():\n    return 7\n")
      (tmp_path/"tests").mkdir()
      (tmp_path/"tests"/"test_route.py").write_text("import app\ndef test_route():\n    assert app.callback() == 7\n")
      def scan(engine, *args, **kwargs):
          return dict(tool="dead", engine="vulture", engine_version="fixture", status="warn", duration_ms=0,
              summary="static candidate", findings=[dict(path=str(source), line=1, rule="vulture",
              severity="warn", message="unused function 'callback'")])
      monkeypatch.setattr(module, "run_engine", scan)
      return dict(confirm_reachability=True, probe_candidate="app.py::callback", probe_tests=["tests/test_route.py"],
          runtime_path=tmp_path/"oci", image_ref="rush@sha256:"+"0"*64, allow_build=True, allow_slow=True)

  def _fake_isolation(monkeypatch, behave):
      calls = []
      fake = types.ModuleType("rush.runtime.isolated_process")
      class IsolationUnavailable(Exception): pass
      def run_isolated_argv(source_root, output_dir, *, runtime_path, image_ref, entrypoint, argv, timeout_s):
          calls.append(argv)
          return behave(Path(source_root), Path(output_dir), IsolationUnavailable)
      fake.IsolationUnavailable, fake.run_isolated_argv = IsolationUnavailable, run_isolated_argv
      monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "rush.runtime.isolated_process", fake)
      return calls

  def _no_scratch(tmp_path):
      assert list(tmp_path.parent.glob(".rush-dead-probe-*")) == []

  def _receipt(out, collected, hits):
      (out/"checks.json").write_text(json.dumps({"collected_tests": collected, "hit_test_ids": hits, "pytest_exit": 0}))
      return subprocess.CompletedProcess(["pytest"], 0, stdout="", stderr="")

  def test_probe_denied_without_grants(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
      args = _probe_project(tmp_path, monkeypatch) | {"allow_build": False, "allow_slow": False}
      calls = _fake_isolation(monkeypatch, lambda *a: pytest.fail("container started"))
      before = _tree(tmp_path)
      result = DeadTool().run(tmp_path, **args)
      assert result["status"] == "error" and result["metadata"]["terminal_reason"] == "permission_denied"
      assert calls == [] and _tree(tmp_path) == before; _no_scratch(tmp_path)

  def test_probe_isolation_unavailable(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
      args = _probe_project(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
      def behave(root, out, unavailable): raise unavailable("no runtime")
      calls = _fake_isolation(monkeypatch, behave); before = _tree(tmp_path)
      result = DeadTool().run(tmp_path, **args)
      assert result["metadata"]["reachability_probe"] == {"status": "skipped", "reason": "isolation_unavailable"}
      assert result["status"] == "warn" and len(calls) == 1 and _tree(tmp_path) == before; _no_scratch(tmp_path)

  def test_probe_malformed_receipt(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
      args = _probe_project(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
      def behave(root, out, unavailable):
          (out/"checks.json").write_text("{"); return subprocess.CompletedProcess(["pytest"], 0, stdout="", stderr="")
      _fake_isolation(monkeypatch, behave); before = _tree(tmp_path)
      result = DeadTool().run(tmp_path, **args)
      assert result["status"] == "error" and result["metadata"]["terminal_reason"] == "invalid_probe_receipt"
      assert _tree(tmp_path) == before; _no_scratch(tmp_path)

  def test_probe_timeout(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
      args = _probe_project(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
      def behave(root, out, unavailable): raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(["pytest"], 300)
      _fake_isolation(monkeypatch, behave); before = _tree(tmp_path)
      result = DeadTool().run(tmp_path, **args)
      assert result["status"] == "error" and result["metadata"]["terminal_reason"] == "timeout"
      assert _tree(tmp_path) == before; _no_scratch(tmp_path)

  def test_probe_path_escape(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
      args = _probe_project(tmp_path, monkeypatch) | {"probe_tests": ["../outside.py"]}
      calls = _fake_isolation(monkeypatch, lambda *a: pytest.fail("container started")); before = _tree(tmp_path)
      result = DeadTool().run(tmp_path, **args)
      assert result["status"] == "error" and result["metadata"]["terminal_reason"] == "probe_path_rejected"
      assert calls == [] and _tree(tmp_path) == before; _no_scratch(tmp_path)

  def test_probe_source_drift(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
      args = _probe_project(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
      def behave(root, out, unavailable):
          (root/"app.py").write_text("def callback():\n    return 8\n")
          return _receipt(out, 1, ["tests/test_route.py::test_route"])
      _fake_isolation(monkeypatch, behave)
      result = DeadTool().run(tmp_path, **args)
      assert result["status"] == "error" and result["metadata"]["terminal_reason"] == "source_drift"
      assert "reject" not in json.dumps(result); _no_scratch(tmp_path)

  def test_probe_inconclusive_when_no_tests_collected(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
      args = _probe_project(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
      _fake_isolation(monkeypatch, lambda root, out, unavailable: _receipt(out, 0, []))
      result = DeadTool().run(tmp_path, **args)
      assert result["metadata"]["reachability_probe"] == {"status": "inconclusive", "reason": "tests_not_completed"}
      _no_scratch(tmp_path)
  ```
  Also replace line 111 `User tree hashes unchanged.` with `_tree(tmp_path) identical before and after every probe case.`

### Missed issues

**M1 — Decorated callbacks never resolve with real Vulture output (major, breaks E1's central case).**
- Evidence: vulture 2.16 on `def register(f):\n    return f\ndef unused():\n    return 1\n@register\ndef callback():\n    return 7\n` printed `app.py:3: unused function 'unused'` and `app.py:5: unused function 'callback'`. Vulture reports the decorator line.
- Python 3.12's `ast` gives `FunctionDef.lineno == 6` for `callback` (decorator at 5). The audit's `n.lineno == finding["line"]` therefore returns `definition_not_resolved`.
- The plan's RED body 3 injects `line=4` (the def line; decorator at line 3), a position real Vulture never reports, so it passes while production fails.
- Fix: match on `finding["line"] in {n.lineno, *(d.lineno for d in n.decorator_list)}`. In RED body 3 change `line=4` to `line=3`, and add `assert row["symbol"] == "callback"` (Q07-09 block 3, Q07-06 test 3a).

**M2 — Knip categories beyond the audit's four are silently dropped (major).**
- Evidence: Knip 6.35.1 JSON for a project with an orphan file and an unused dependency returned `{'file':'orphan.js','files':[{'name':'orphan.js'}]}` and `{'file':'package.json','dependencies':[{'name':'left-pad'}]}`. Another project returned `binaries`, `devDependencies`, `unlisted` and `unresolved` entries (the latter two with `line`), and `duplicates` as a list of lists.
- The audit's normalizer iterates only exports/types/enumMembers/namespaceMembers, so such a project still reports `ok` with 0 findings. That is the same masking class as R1, and the CLI docs say "Find unused code and dependencies".
- Fix: included in Q07-01's categories text and code.

**M3 — Engine entry scope is wrong for both engines after Q07-01 (major, folded into Q07-02's fix).**
- `_entry_scope` (`subprocesses.py` at 66c6c79) derives coverage from argv file targets and `consumed_paths`.
- Today Vulture reports `unavailable/requested_files_unknown` (no `consumed_paths`). After the Knip positional removal, Knip would report `none` while it ran.
- Fix: the `consumed_paths` plus `_with_child_scope` text in Q07-02.

**M4 — No owner for dead's option declarations (major).**
- Plans 02, 03 and 05 list `src/rush/catalog.py` option declarations in their own deliverables (`02:173`, `03:225`, `05:225`). Plan 04 assigns `TOOL_SPECS` to Foundation (`04:116`). Plan 07 says nothing.
- At 66c6c79 dead needs `ToolSpec("dead").option_specs` and `_TOOL_CLI_OPTIONS["dead"]`. Q07-11 and Q07-13 fix text now names both; the plan must assign an owner.

**M5 — Source drift must be re-checked after the run (major).**
- Plan lines 58-59 require "source drift invalidates result". The audit compares the digest only before the run (audit lines 3410-3412). Covered by `source_drift` in Q07-09 block 4 and `test_probe_source_drift` in Q07-12.

**M6 — Digest scope is ambiguous (minor).**
- The plan says "exact definition path/name/line and SHA256" and calls the field `definition_digest`, but the audit hashes the whole file (`hashlib.sha256(source.read_bytes())`, audit line 3375).
- A whole-file digest expires every exception on any edit to the file, not only the definition.
- Options, both full scope: (A) whole-file SHA-256, name the field accordingly; (B) SHA-256 of `ast.get_source_segment(source, definition)`, so exceptions survive unrelated edits.

**M7 — Probe/early-exit errors discard static findings (minor).**

#### Q08-04 — Trial fixture `a.js` gives jscpd `sources=0`; the directory protocol also scans the wrong set
- Severity: blocker.
- Plan location: 08-rush-complexity.md:46-53 (jscpd protocol), 228 (`a.js`), 246 (`== (0,0)`).
- Problem:
  - jscpd 5.2.0 drops files below its token threshold from `statistics.total.sources`. The plan's own rule (lines 51-52) then turns the trial fixture into an error, so `verified_candidate` is unreachable.
  - Lines 49-50 give the wrong cause. File operands analyze fine when files are token-rich; zero sources comes from the threshold, not the operand type.
  - The finding missed that a bare directory scan (the plan's chosen protocol) scans the wrong file set.
- Evidence (all jscpd 5.2.0, exit 0):
  - Trial fixture directory: `sources 0`.
  - Two 7-line `export const` files: `sources 0` as a directory, and `sources 0` as file operands.
  - Two token-rich 7-line files as file operands: `sources 2, clones 1`.
  - Seven distinct `export function valueN(a, b) { return a + b * N - (a / b); }` lines: `sources 1, clones 0`.
  - A directory holding Python duplicates plus a JS file: formats `['javascript','python']`, `sources 3, clones 1`. With `--format javascript,jsx,typescript,tsx`: `sources 1, clones 0`.
  - A directory with duplicate files in `src/`, `node_modules/`, `dist/` and `.venv/`: `sources 4, clones 3` (vendored trees counted). With `--ignore "**/node_modules/**,**/.venv/**,**/dist/**"`: `sources 2, clones 1`. `--ignore "**/.*/**"` excludes hidden dirs.
  - The report holds only `duplicates` and `statistics`, with no per-file list.
  - `mjs`, `cjs` and `ts` files all count under `--format javascript,jsx,typescript,tsx`.
- Fix for Codex (three edits):
  1. Replace line 228:
     ```python
         (tmp_path/"src/a.js").write_text("".join(
             f"export function value{i}(a, b) {{ return a + b * {i} - (a / b); }}\n"
             for i in range(7)))
     ```
  2. Replace plan lines 46-53 (from "Jscpd uses --reporters json" through "…including zero-source case.") with:
     ```text
     Jscpd runs `jscpd --reporters json --output <invocation-owned dir> --format
     javascript,jsx,typescript,tsx --ignore "<**/NAME/** for every NAME in
     tools/routing.py::_SKIP_DIRS>,**/.*/**" <contained dir>` and parses the actual
     jscpd-report.json (statistics.total, duplicates). The format and ignore flags make
     the scanned set equal Rush's collected JS/TS set; without them a directory scan
     also counts Python files and node_modules/.venv/dist trees. Require exit 0,
     statistics.total.sources int, clones == len(duplicates). jscpd drops files below
     its default token threshold from sources (default --min-tokens/--min-lines are
     never lowered), and the report lists no per-file sources, so: sources==0 with
     declared JS/TS targets => error_result(..., terminal_reason=
     "zero_assessed_sources") and ComplexityTool sets metadata.unassessed_paths to
     every declared target; 0<sources<len(declared) => ok/warn with
     metadata.assessed_files=sources and metadata.declared_files=len(declared);
     never clean on zero. Direct file operands analyze files that clear the token
     threshold; they were not the cause of the observed "Files analyzed 0".
     Commit captured jscpd 5.2.0 reports (see Q08-24).
     ```
  3. In `test_malformed_reports_not_clean`, add `sources:0` to the jscpd loop and assert `metadata["terminal_reason"] == "zero_assessed_sources"` for it. Add `test_jscpd_argv_scopes_to_declared_js_ts`. It monkeypatches `rush.engines.jscpd.run_subprocess` to capture argv and `resolve_binary` to `lambda _b: "jscpd"`. It asserts `"--format"` is followed by `"javascript,jsx,typescript,tsx"` and `"--ignore"` is followed by a value containing `"**/node_modules/**"` and `"**/.*/**"`.
- Fix verification: after implementing, run `jscpd --reporters json --output <mktemp -d> --format javascript,jsx,typescript,tsx <fixture dir>` and confirm `sources 1`. Then `rtk grep -n "zero_assessed_sources" docs/phase-plans/command-tdd-2026-10-01/08-rush-complexity.md` shows a RED assertion.

#### Q08-17 — Real Radon JSON shape not handled; the finding's closure rule is wrong
- Severity: major.
- Plan location: 08-rush-complexity.md:44-45, 139-140.
- Problem: radon 6.0.1 emits a class row whose complexity aggregates its methods, and each method appears twice (nested in `methods` and again at top level). A syntax-error file gives `{"file.py":{"error":…}}`, a dict rather than a list. Closure rows are nested under their function and their complexity is not included in the enclosing function's.
- Evidence (executed):
  - Class `C` with methods `m` (2) and `n` (1) gives rows `class C 3`, `method m 2`, `method n 1` at top level, plus `methods:[m, n]` nested under the class. Summing everything gives 6 against a true 3.
  - `radon cc --json bad.py` gives `{"bad.py": {"error": "invalid syntax (<unknown>, line 1)"}}`.
  - `def outer(a): def inner(b): …` gives `outer complexity 2` and a nested `closures:[inner complexity 2]`. `radon cc -s` prints only `F 1:0 outer - A (2)`.
- Fix for Codex: insert after line 45:
  ```text
  Metric rows and totals sum each executable unit exactly once: top-level items with type
  "function" or "method" (symbol "Class.method" when classname is present) plus every
  entry reachable through their "closures" lists (a closure's complexity is not part of
  its parent's). type "class" rows and each class row's nested "methods" list are never
  summed (their methods already appear as top-level rows). A file value of the form
  {"error": str} is a per-file parse failure: error_result(..., terminal_reason=
  "source_parse_error"), the failing path in metadata.unassessed_paths, and other files'
  rows are kept as metadata.metrics.
  ```
  Add REDs: the class payload gives rows `[("C.m",2),("C.n",1)]` and total 3; the closure payload gives `[("outer",2),("outer.inner",2)]` and total 4; `{"bad.py":{"error":"x"}}` gives `status error` and `terminal_reason == "source_parse_error"`.
- Fix verification: `rtk grep -n "source_parse_error\|closures" docs/phase-plans/command-tdd-2026-10-01/08-rush-complexity.md`.

### Missed issues (same evidence standard)

1. **jscpd directory scan scope contamination (blocker-class, folded into Q08-04).** Without `--format` and `--ignore`, the plan's chosen directory protocol counts Python files and `node_modules`/`.venv`/`dist`, so `duplicated_lines` and `sources` stop matching the declared JS/TS set. Evidence: the four jscpd runs listed under Q08-04. The rewritten Q08-04 includes the flags and a unit RED on argv.
2. **Docs CI gate.** `scripts/sync_docs.py --check` (`ci.yml:67`) fails on any changed or new doc whose digest is not recorded in `docs/reports/phase-64-66-documentation-coverage.md`, and on contract drift for `complexity`. The plan and the finding set never mention it. Fixed in Q08-02 and Q08-29.
3. **Stale catalog metadata and an unlisted consumer.**
   - `src/rush/catalog.py:232` has `engine_names=("radon","jscpd")`.
   - Its `mcp_description` (`catalog.py:229-230`) and `ComplexityTool.mcp_description` (`complexity.py:17`) say "radon or jscpd; missing … returns skipped", while five engines run.
   - `src/rush/workflows/suites.py:49` runs `complexity` in a gate suite (`tests/test_workflows.py:36` asserts it).
   - The plan's status changes (jscpd zero-source error, radon strict, ok+skipped warn) change what that suite sees.
   - Required: update `catalog.py` `engine_names` and both descriptions, and add a regression assertion on the suite's handling of `warn`/`error` complexity statuses (investigation needed: read `workflows/` status handling before choosing the assertion).
4. **Sandbox behavior for non-root targets.** `PatchSandboxManager(root)` uses `root = path` (resolved). `git worktree add --detach … HEAD` (`sandbox.py:70-73`) checks out the whole repository at HEAD, so for a subdirectory target the trial's `/work` is the whole repo, and uncommitted target changes are ignored. The audit's `TemporaryDirectory(dir=root.parent)` (audit 3711) writes outside the target root; see D4. The plan states neither; add a RED with a subdirectory target that asserts the receipt records the actual scanned root.
5. **Internal contradiction in the plan.** Line 55 says metric rows retain "engine, function/location, value, unit and source digest". The line-134 schema and the test rows (lines 197-200) have `{path,symbol,metric,unit,value}` only. Resolved by D5 plus the row shape used in Q08-06/Q08-14.
6. **Unvalidated clines report shape.** clines is not installed here, so no real report exists to ground any clines metric row. Covered in Q08-24.

## Plan 09 — rush_slop (09-rush-slop.md)


Verified 20 of 20 findings against primary sources at c78e445 and 66c6c79. No file was written. P below means `docs/phase-plans/command-tdd-2026-10-01/09-rush-slop.md`.

**Disclosure.** I made one probe mistake. My first in-memory test of a patch bound `engine_on_path` and `run_engine` in the wrong namespace, so the real installed aislop ran once against a `tempfile` directory. It ran under default grants. At 66c6c79 `AislopEngine.child_env` sets `npm_config_offline=true` when the download grant is absent (aislop.py, `child_env`), so no download was possible. Free space stayed at 21 GiB, the temp dir was deleted, and `git status` is clean in the phase-70 worktree. Every later probe mocked the Python engine.

What I ran, for context:
- In-process runs of the plan's RED bodies at both revisions.
- Live stdio MCP probes and CLI runs, using JS-only temp dirs.
- Live `sloppylint 0.5.1` runs.
- In-memory execution of the proposed patches inside the 66c6c79 `rush.tools.slop` namespace.
- `scripts/sync_docs.py --check`.

#### Q09-08 — `test_engine_crash_not_clean` has no body; protocol tests assert status only
- Severity: major.
- Plan location: P:93–94 (names `test_engine_crash_not_clean`), P:152–157 (only malformed cases, status only).
- Evidence: the in-process table under Q09-03. The audit (:3832) requires a silent-nonzero test. The finding's proposed bodies were run in memory against the patched `SloppylintEngine.normalize`:
  - exit 0 with `{`, `[]`, `{"issues": {}}`, `{"issues": [1]}` or empty stdout gives `error` with summary `sloppylint produced no valid JSON report (exit 0)`.
  - exit 2 with `Traceback: boom` gives `...(exit 2): Traceback: boom`.
  - The aislop `diagnostics-0.16.1.json` fixture gives `fail` with 3 findings. A silent aislop exit 1 gives `error`, summary `aislop produced no JSON report (exit 1)`.
  - The existing `sloppylint.json` fixture gives `warn` with `[("src/example.py",12,"verbose-comment","warn")]`.
- Fix for Codex: this is rewritten. The finding's body had a dead expression (`"fail" if False else "warn"`) and a redundant membership assertion. Replace P:152–157 and add the crash test:
```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "engine_reports"

def _sloppylint(monkeypatch):
    engine = SloppylintEngine()
    monkeypatch.setattr(engine, "version", lambda: "0.5.1")
    return engine

def test_malformed_engine_output_is_error(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    engine = _sloppylint(monkeypatch)
    clean = engine.normalize({"exit_code": 0, "stdout": (FIXTURES/"sloppylint-clean-0.5.1.json").read_text(), "stderr": ""}, tmp_path, "slop")
    assert (clean["status"], clean["findings"]) == ("ok", [])
    found = engine.normalize({"exit_code": 0, "stdout": (FIXTURES/"sloppylint.json").read_text(), "stderr": ""}, tmp_path, "slop")
    assert (found["status"], [(f["path"], f["line"], f["rule"], f["severity"]) for f in found["findings"]]) == (
        "warn", [("src/example.py", 12, "verbose-comment", "warn")])
    invalid = "sloppylint produced no valid JSON report (exit 0)"
    for stdout in ("{", "[]", '{"issues": {}}', '{"issues": [1]}', ""):
        out = engine.normalize({"exit_code": 0, "stdout": stdout, "stderr": ""}, tmp_path, "slop")
        assert (out["status"], out["summary"], out["findings"]) == ("error", invalid, [])
    aislop = AislopEngine(); monkeypatch.setattr(aislop, "version", lambda: "0.16.1")
    report = json.loads((FIXTURES/"aislop"/"diagnostics-0.16.1.json").read_text())
    result = aislop.normalize({"exit_code": 1, "parsed": report, "findings": report["diagnostics"], "stderr": "", "cwd": str(tmp_path)}, tmp_path, "slop")
    assert result["status"] == "fail" and len(result["findings"]) == 3  # fixture: 2 error + 1 warning diagnostics
    bad = aislop.normalize({"exit_code": 0, "stdout": "{", "parsed": None, "findings": []}, tmp_path, "slop")
    assert (bad["status"], bad["summary"]) == ("error", "aislop produced no JSON report (exit 0)")

def test_engine_crash_not_clean(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    engine = _sloppylint(monkeypatch)
    crash = json.loads((FIXTURES/"sloppylint-process-failure-0.5.1.json").read_text())
    out = engine.normalize(crash, tmp_path, "slop")
    assert (out["status"], out["findings"]) == ("error", [])
    assert out["summary"].startswith("sloppylint produced no valid JSON report (exit 2): ")
    assert "unrecognized arguments" in out["summary"]
    silent = engine.normalize({"exit_code": 2, "stdout": "", "stderr": ""}, tmp_path, "slop")
    assert (silent["status"], silent["summary"]) == ("error", "sloppylint produced no valid JSON report (exit 2)")
    aislop = AislopEngine(); monkeypatch.setattr(aislop, "version", lambda: "0.16.1")
    quiet = aislop.normalize({"exit_code": 1, "parsed": None, "findings": [], "stderr": ""}, tmp_path, "slop")
    assert (quiet["status"], quiet["summary"]) == ("error", "aislop produced no JSON report (exit 1)")
```

#### Q09-10 — Project-style config contract drifted from the audit and is underspecified
- Severity: major.
- Verdict: CORRECTED. The finding's claim that no typed catalog-config mechanism exists is wrong. Everything else holds.
- Plan location: P:46–57, P:122.
- What holds:
  - The audit puts the config at `.rush/slop-rules.json` (:3878–3884), and its default-location CLI example `rush slop src --rule-profile project_style` (:3911) needs that default. The plan dropped it silently.
  - P:47–49 includes `message` but never says whether it is required, while the calibration candidate `{id,literal}` (P:59) must be a valid entry.
  - `source_config_digest` is not a `Finding` key at either revision (`base.py` Finding keys). 66c6c79 adds `extensions: dict[str, Any]` (`base.py:55-58`), which is absent at c78e445. Strict `validate_finding` rejects unknown top-level keys (`contracts/results.py:210-217`, `FINDING_KEYS` :33-52 includes `extensions`).
  - The CLI and MCP JSON output pass legacy dicts through unchanged: I observed `extensions`, `rule_id` and even stray top-level keys preserved. The digest placement is therefore a typing and strict-contract question, not a transport one.
- What the finding got wrong: `ToolConfig` does have `options: Mapping[str, ToolOptionValue]` (`config.py:47-50`). `ToolSpec.option_specs` of `ToolOptionSpec` (value types str/int/float/bool/tuple, `path_kind`) declares typed options. `resolve_tool_options` (`config.py:279`) applies default, then config, then invocation, and `tools/mutation.py:168-187` is the in-repo pattern. P:56–57 ("only through declared typed option") refers to exactly this. I verified in memory that declaring `ToolOptionSpec(name="rule_config_path", value_type=str, default=None, path_kind="file")` on `TOOL_SPECS["slop"]` makes `[tools.slop] rule_config_path="cfg/rules.json"` load. An undeclared key is rejected ("unknown option 'bogus'"), a wrong type is rejected ("must be str, got int"), and an explicit invocation value overrides config. Pass only non-None invocation options, because `resolve_tool_options("slop", opts, {"rule_config_path": None})` returns `None`.
- Fix for Codex: replace P:46–57, from `project_style accepts` through `CLI override precedence explicit.`, with
```
project_style config: UTF-8 JSON object with exactly the keys "version" and "rules";
"version" is int 1 (bool rejected); "rules" is a list of objects with required non-empty
strings "id" (unique) and "literal" and an optional non-empty string "message", no other
keys. An empty list is valid and yields zero rule findings (audit :3893-3896; decision D4).
Location: `rule_config_path` when given, else `.rush/slop-rules.json` under the scan root
when that file exists (audit :3878-3884); both resolved per the path rule. Catalog
configuration: TOOL_SPECS["slop"].option_specs gains ToolOptionSpec(name="rule_config_path",
value_type=str, default=None, path_kind="file", description=...), so `[tools.slop]
rule_config_path = "..."` is a declared typed option (config.py:152-163 parses it,
config.py:279 resolve_tool_options applies default -> config -> invocation, same pattern
as tools/mutation.py:168-187); an explicit CLI/MCP value wins; config is read only when
rule_profile is "project_style" and no explicit path was given. Each case-sensitive
substring match per line over the selected Python and JS/TS files (text read as UTF-8,
errors="ignore", as in the marker pass) yields Finding {path, line, rule: <id>, rule_id:
<id>, severity: "warn", message: <rule message, else "project-style literal match:
<literal>">, extensions: {"source_config_digest": <sha256 of the exact config bytes>}}. The
digest is under `extensions`, the Finding TypedDict's declared open field (base.py:55-58
at 66c6c79; absent at c78e445, so Q09 lands on the phase/70 base), because a top-level
key fails mypy and strict validate_finding. metadata.project_style = {"status":
"assessed","source_config_digest":d,"rules":[ids]} and metadata.rule_config_digest = d
(audit :3905). A project_style row {"language":"project_style","engine":"rush","rules":[ids],
"paths":[selected files],"status":"warn" if matches else "ok"} joins metadata.assessed; with
zero selected files its status is "skipped". No config => metadata.project_style =
```
